answer: Each identity must cross a glacier, a slow field of real work. Honest identities leave deep footprints; a farm's are identical. Every identity needs a haven, a port where its work is inspected. Honest havens are many; a farm's ships dock at one pier, at one hour. Trust is earned by writing a sonnet, a strict form that cannot be copied - each line must fit the meter. Honest sonnets are all different; a farm's are the same fourteen lines. To pass, a farm must cross a real glacier, dock at a different haven, and write a real sonnet for every sockpuppet.
